name: Aegis Logistics Ltd
title: Aegis Logistics Ltd - 500003 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 with LPG distribution margin ~INR7,000/t vs ~INR4,000 prior year, but management attributes it to a war-driven price spike and guides capex up sharply (~$1.2bn by Mar-27, ~INR5,000cr in FY28) with no numeric utilisation disclosed for terminals.

summary.headline: Aegis Logistics FY26 PAT rose 41% to INR1,107 crore and Q4 PAT rose 43% to INR455 crore, led by LPG distribution margins of about INR7,000 per ton.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 23% to INR8,333 crore, normalized EBITDA rose 36% to INR1,599 crore, and PAT crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 52% to INR2,594 crore and normalized EBITDA up 54% to INR670 crore. The LPG segment drove the result, with distribution volumes up 45% in FY26 and 71% in Q4, while the Liquid segment was flat on revenue and EBITDA fell 5% for the year. Management outlined a large capex pipeline (about $1.2 billion to March 2027, about INR5,000 crore in FY28, about $5 billion through 2030/31) and said it expects to maintain FY27 momentum.

segments.name: LPG
segments.commentary: FY26 terminal throughput reached 5.15 million tons (+14%), distribution volumes 7.54 lakh MT (+45%) and sourcing sales 6.07 lakh MT (+2%). Q4 LPG revenue INR2,410 crore (+65%) and EBITDA INR549 crore (+136%), with Q4 distribution volume at a record 2.34 lakh MT (+71%).

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR644 crore and EBITDA INR472 crore (-5%), reflecting phasing of capacity additions and no major take-or-pay contribution versus last year. Q4 revenue INR184 crore and EBITDA INR126 crore.

guidance_outlook: Distribution margin guided at about INR7,000 per ton, which management expects to sustain through FY27 and beyond; FY26 average was about INR7,000 versus about INR4,000 in FY25.

Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion by March 2027; about INR5,000 crore capex in FY28; about $5 billion pipeline through 2030/31 (management clarified the target is December 2030 and that heavy spending falls in FY29-FY31).
Long-term EPS CAGR guidance of about 25% reiterated; management said it is conservative and that it has beaten its own guidance.
Target of about 2 million tons of gas distribution (LPG plus ammonia) by FY28.

Ammonia: expected utilization about 25% in year one, then growing 30-40% a year; ammonia throughput margin INR2,500-3,000 per ton; distribution about 200,000 tons initially, growing 20-30% a year, margin up to INR5,000 per ton.
LPG supply shortfall improved from about 50% in April to about 30% in May; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 but declined to forecast precisely.
risks_watch: Distribution margin sustainability: the INR7,000 per ton level is tied to elevated energy prices and the war; management says it expects scale-driven procurement gains from FY28 but offered no quantified path.
LPG supply normalization: shortfall still about 30% in May; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 with no firm date.
Execution timing: JNPT, Mumbai, Kandla CRL 4, Pipavav jetty and ammonia terminal, and Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline are all targeted for H1 FY27 or year-end FY27; slippage would delay volumes.
Capex step-up from about INR800 crore in FY26 to about $1.2 billion by March 2027 and about $5 billion by 2030; funding mix and gearing (about 0.6x) to watch.
Vadhavan port (about INR20,000 crore) remains a nonbinding MoU subject to approvals and land allocation; its inclusion in the capex pipeline is uncertain.
Ammonia economics are new and unproven for the company; utilization and margin targets are management estimates.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on growth and the energy-transition opportunity, but conservative on numbers: management declined to raise the 25% EPS CAGR guidance and said it prefers to under-promise. Evasive on exact timing of LPG normalization and on precise FY28-30 ammonia volumes.
key_quotes: We are a very conservative company and I think 25% CAGR growth is not small.
Going forward, we feel the INR7,000-odd margins should be sustainable as beyond '26, '27, we would see our distribution volumes really of a scale that brings procurement efficiencies.
So, we are very bullish. We have a partner, Itochu, along with us.
our sort of philosophy here at Aegis is really to not to overpromise, always to under promise, and hopefully overdeliver.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q4 jump in gas segment profitability per ton, was there a one-off, and what is the normalized level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin averaged about INR7,000/MT vs INR4,000 in the prior year, with volume surge also contributing; it expects INR7,000-odd to be sustainable as scale brings procurement efficiencies, and full-year effects of Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals will add to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: When will LPG supply fully normalize, and what is the FY27 and FY28 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: LPG shortfall fell from about 50% in April to about 30% in May; normalcy is expected sometime in Q2. Capex is about $1.2 billion by March 2027 and about INR5,000 crore in FY28, both organic and inorganic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vadhavan MoU included in the capex pipeline, and what is the exact capex split of FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Vadhavan could be included in the $5 billion pipeline depending on land allotment and permits, but not all of it. The $5 billion is through December 2030 (not FY30), with heavy spend in FY29-FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ammonia economics for utilization and margins, and does ammonia distribution reach INR5,000/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilization is expected at about 25% in year one, then growing 30-40% a year; throughput margin INR2,500-3,000/MT; distribution starts at about 200,000 tons, growing 20-30% a year, with margin up to INR5,000/MT depending on the market.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from volumes versus price, and how will revenue trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of the rise from about INR4,000 to INR7,000 comes from volume-led procurement efficiencies (volumes went from about 5.2 lakh to 7.5 lakh MT) and part from margin improvement; it expects revenue to grow year on year as volume offsets price normalization.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the 25% EPS CAGR guidance, and what are the FY30 ammonia and LPG volume targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conservative, has beaten its own guidance, and achieved 32% EPS CAGR over five years; EPS has moved from INR6 to INR26 with the CAGR guidance unchanged. It declined to give a precise FY30 ammonia volume, citing dependence on terminals commissioned and locations secured, but pointed to a 3 million ton ammonia supply-demand gap by 2029 per CRISIL.

capex_capacity: Mumbai: 64,000 kL additional liquid storage at INR125 crore project cost, commissioning targeted H1 FY27; facility currently 334,000 kL liquid and 21,000 MT static LPG

JNPT: liquid storage 106,900 cbm; expansion of ~318,100 cbm liquid, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and 35,000 MT annual LPG bottling plant, total outlay ~INR1,675 crore; first liquid phase targeted H1 FY27; evaluating 36,000-50,000 MT cryogenic tank

Kandla: ~952,000 cbm liquid and 48,000 MT LPG; VLGC-compliant after December 2025 handling; Jamnagar-Loni LPG pipeline complete; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection targeted H1 FY27; CRL 4 liquid terminal adding 94,148 cbm with commissioning targeted next year; nonbinding MoU with L&T for ammonia terminals

Pipavav: 48,000 MT cryogenic LPG terminal commissioned June 2025, total LPG 70,800 MT; new VLGC jetty targeted within calendar 2026 with KGPL pipeline connection in Q2 FY27; 15-year take-or-pay for petroleum products with committed volumes above 0.5 million MT per year, operations by year-end; 36,000 MT ammonia terminal backed by 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc, commissioning targeted H1 FY27; Itochu holds 10% in Aegis Terminal Pipavav, intends to reach 25% over 3 years

Haldia: 75% stake in Hindustan Aegis LPG acquired adding ~25,000 MT LPG storage, 226,890 cbm liquid storage, exclusive terminaling agreement with HPCL through 2038; 3 acres added. Mangalore: 82,000 MT cryogenic LPG terminal commissioned June 2025; 75,000 cbm liquid added and fully operational; further 60,000 cbm under evaluation. Kochi: 82,545 cbm, evaluating 60,000 cbm more. Vadhavan: nonbinding MoU, potential ~INR20,000 crore investment subject to approvals and land

Capex: cumulative ~$1.2 billion by March 2027; ~INR5,000 crore in FY28 (organic and inorganic); ~$5 billion pipeline through December 2030, with heavy spend in FY29-FY31; FY26 capex about INR800 crore per analyst; gearing target ~0.6x funded by equity, internal accruals and debt
demand_pricing: LPG distribution volumes 7.54 lakh MT in FY26 (+45%) and record 2.34 lakh MT in Q4 (+71%); distribution volume rose from about 5.2 lakh to 7.5 lakh MT per management

Distribution margin averaged about INR7,000/MT in FY26 vs about INR4,000 in FY25; Q1 FY27 margin also strong; management expects INR7,000 to sustain as procurement efficiencies from scale arrive in FY28
LPG terminal throughput 5.15 million MT in FY26 (+14%); Q4 throughput 1.23 million MT, flat despite West Asia disruption; sourcing sales 6.07 lakh MT (+2%)
LPG supply shortfall about 50% in April and about 30% in May 2026; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 without a firm forecast; supply diversified to Canada, US, Argentina, Nigeria

Ammonia: one-third of Pipavav ammonia capacity under take-or-pay (Hindustan Zinc), two-thirds open for the company to sell; expected utilization ~25% in year one, rising 30-40% a year; throughput margin INR2,500-3,000/MT; distribution starting ~200,000 tons, growing 20-30% a year, margin up to INR5,000/MT

Energy product prices moved from about INR54,000-60,000/MT pre-war to as high as INR150,000/MT and then about INR80,000-90,000/MT; management says inventory is held under about one month and no inventory gain is booked

adds.what: 64,000 kL additional liquid storage at Mumbai (INR125 crore)
JNPT expansion ~318,100 cbm liquid, 77,236 MT LPG and 35,000 MT bottling plant (~INR1,675 crore outlay)
Pipavav 36,000 MT ammonia terminal backed by 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc

growth.why: Management expects to maintain FY27 momentum, with INR7,000/t distribution margin guided to sustain and ~$1.2bn capex by Mar-27 plus INR5,000 cr in FY28; capacity additions (Mumbai, JNPT, Pipavav, Kandla) are partly specified with H1 FY27 timelines, but no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given.
